scope: Vietnamese personal-care need parsing and multi-turn catalog consultation
changes: Recognize common frequency modifiers hay and thuong in skin, scalp, and hair condition phrases.
Keep short causal or temporal context attached to the stated need instead of treating it as product-search text.
Use the active catalog product family on preference-only follow-ups and state when catalog evidence cannot verify suitability.
Render singular results as one product and avoid appending a redundant generic unverified-fact sentence.

limitations: The product snapshot does not verify whether a listed item is clinically or cosmetically suitable for a particular skin or hair condition; the response explicitly abstains from that claim.
This is a deterministic local snapshot evaluation, not a human-rated blind study, live-stock check, provider reliability test, browser E2E, or production load test.
No product-specific SKU rule or catalog record was changed.
